en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ekacintika Kuṭajapupphiyavagga 7 I was once a forest-dwelling sage, living in the depths of the woods. At that time, a king named Mahāsena reigned over the earth. He possessed a hundred thousand chariots and a hundred thousand elephants; His wealth was vast, his power great, and he ruled over the entire world. One day, while wandering through the forest, I saw a man who had fallen ill; With a compassionate heart, I approached him and spoke these words: "O man, what is your ailment? What is the cause of your suffering? "I am afflicted by a severe illness," he replied, "and I have no medicine. Hearing his words, I felt great pity and took him to my own abode. There, I provided him with food and drink, and I tended to his every need. When he recovered from his sickness, I gave him a single *kuṭaja* flower. Having offered it with a devout mind, I made this aspiration: "By this merit, may I become a Buddha in the future, And may I lead all beings across the ocean of saṃsāra. Through that root of merit, I have attained the state of an Arhat; I have fulfilled my purpose and am now free from all defilements. Having seen the Truth, I have reached the end of suffering; I am now cool and peaceful, having attained final Nibbāna. Thus did the Elder Ekacintika speak of his past deeds. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Ekacintika.
“When a god passes away from the host of gods at the exhaustion of his lifespan,
three sounds resound:”
Rejoicing in the gods:
"O sir, go from here to a happy destination,
to the company of human beings."
Having become a human being, obtain supreme faith in the true Dhamma.
May that faith of yours be firmly established.
Rooted and firmly established,
they remain unshakable for as long as life lasts in the well-proclaimed True Dharma.
Having performed wholesome deeds with the body,
having performed much wholesome deeds with speech,
and having performed wholesome deeds with the mind,
Free from ill will and without attachment.
Then, having performed much merit based on acquisitions through giving;
Establish other people as well in the true Dhamma and in the holy life.
Out of this compassion, [establish them].
When the gods know a god is passing away,
they rejoice and say:
"Come back, O god, again and again!"
At that time, when the assembly of gods had gathered, a sense of spiritual urgency arose within me:
"Into what kind of womb, indeed, shall I enter?"
Having passed away from here, I shall go [to that state].
Perceiving my sense of spiritual urgency,
the ascetic with developed faculties—
Desiring to rescue me,
he came into my presence;
his name was Sumanas.
A disciple of Padumuttara,
having instructed me in the eightfold Dhamma,
then inspired me with a sense of spiritual urgency.
Having heard his words,
I gained confidence in the Buddha;
having paid homage to that steadfast one, I—
There I passed away;
impelled by the root of my wholesome merit, I was reborn right there.
For a hundred thousand eons,
I did not fall into an evil rebirth.
I possess the four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā).
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Ekacintika Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Ekacintika is the seventh.
